name: MMT-Bench
intro: MMT-Bench 是大型视觉语言模型多任务能力基准，包含 31,325 道多模态多选题、32 个元任务和 162 个子任务，覆盖 13 类视觉输入与 14 类能力。论文 v1 通过 OpenCompass 的三级答案抽取评测 30 个公开可用 LVLM，并以 162 个 LoRA 任务向量构建分层任务地图。
org: Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, The University of Hong Kong, The University of Adelaide, Zhejiang University, Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
build_method: 多源数据, 规则生成, ChatGPT生成
modality: 图像, 文本, 视频, 点云
task_type: 多模态理解, 多任务评测
eval_feature: 多任务, 任务地图, 视觉识别定位推理规划
scale: 31,325个多模态多选题, 32个元任务, 162个子任务
build_method_en: Multi-source data, rule generation, ChatGPT generation
intro_en: MMT-Bench evaluates large vision-language models across 31,325 multimodal multiple-choice questions, 32 meta-tasks, 162 subtasks, 13 visual input types, and 14 capability types. Paper v1 evaluates 30 publicly available LVLMs with OpenCompass three-stage answer extraction and builds a hierarchical task map from 162 LoRA task vectors.

drawio_review_note: Primary-source audit pins the sole paper revision arXiv:2404.16006v1 (2024-04-24; PDF SHA-256 386e96e079eb0cc4ac0d7ef5700e4f924780975cebaef62b4afa6828b0ad3ee1), the first public evaluation-code commit 8ec8203c44b420d299e01a5f74410455da34a52d (2024-04-26), the post-release evaluator update e700458829d134ece339b65731d5aae988be1fe5, the current official repository commit 5e900028e8bc5636ce31dd263e975e3882c29f82, the public OpenGVLab/MMT-Bench Hugging Face snapshot 2255d3a7b250ae6d87383dbb9ab0d6416432ece7, and the full-annotation release tag commit 84012c95e31c2986521ea5b7c16a88e36e9958c2. paper_url and arxiv_pdf_url are locked to v1; the 32-model claim previously shown on this page was incorrect for the paper, whose abstract, Section 4, and Appendix L all specify 30 LVLMs. All coauthors brainstorm candidate meta-tasks, deduplicate them, and filter for importance to retain 32. Candidate subtasks are retained only when they test a fundamental multimodal capability, challenge current LVLMs, and have publicly accessible test samples, producing 162 subtasks. Dozens of AI-specialist coauthors conduct data collection. For each subtask they search Google, Papers With Code, Kaggle, and ChatGPT, download candidates, and assess relevance and usability. Random sampling caps each subtask at 200 examples and assigns equal sample counts to each contributing dataset. Uniform metadata contains images plus information needed to generate QA, with manual annotations of required capabilities and visual-prompt/input-image types. Depending on the subtask, manually designed rules or well-designed ChatGPT prompts generate a gold answer and at most eight choices; the paper gives random distractor-image sampling for sketch-to-image retrieval and ChatGPT-generated confusing distractors for video captioning as examples. The final paper benchmark has 31,325 multimodal multiple-choice questions, 32 meta-tasks, 162 subtasks, 13 visual input types, and 14 capability types. Paper-v1 evaluation covers 30 publicly available LVLMs. Its OpenCompass protocol first checks for an option letter, then option content, then uses ChatGPT; if all three fail or a model refuses/answers unclearly, the paper assigns Z to avoid random assignment, and Z is incorrect. Accuracy is the primary metric. Table 2 states that Overall is computed across all subtasks and Overall* excludes visual recognition; the paper's broader-impact limitation explicitly states that each meta-task score is the average over all its subtasks. The first public evaluator instead uses row-level means for overall, meta-task, and subtask accuracy. Commit e7004588 aligns meta-task aggregation with the paper by changing it to an unweighted mean of subtask accuracies while retaining a row-level overall mean; the paper gives the scope of Overall but no explicit row-versus-subtask weighting equation. The official evaluator also conflicts with the paper's failure contract: local letter/content inference runs first, the ChatGPT judge retries up to three times, and exhaustion randomly selects from valid choices plus Z with seed 2680 instead of deterministically returning Z; this behavior exists in the first public code and remains in the current vendored evaluator. The same code accepts all uppercase option columns during local inference but hard-codes the English and Chinese ChatGPT judge prompts to A–D even though construction allows up to eight choices; the paper-level flow therefore stays option-generic and records A–D only as implementation drift. For task-map analysis, the paper first selects pretrained Qwen-VL-Chat as the probe model because its initial weights perform well on most subtasks; second, it adapts every subtask's MCQs into instruction-following data; third, it LoRA-fine-tunes the probe for three epochs separately on all 162 subtasks; each 3.5M-parameter weight delta is a task vector; pairwise distance is one minus cosine similarity in the range 0–2; hierarchical clustering with 12 clusters and Kendall tau ranking consistency support in-domain/out-of-domain analysis. The pinned HF snapshot is public, declares CC BY 4.0, and contains four files: 10% validation and full sets, each in a combined-image and an MI variant preserving separate multi-images. Full-set evaluation was originally server-hosted; the later all_anno tag exposes full annotations. The official repository root has no benchmark-level LICENSE file even though its vendored VLMEvalKit subtree contains a separate license. Candidate-task/data counts, exact deduplication and rejection rules, QA review/adjudication, ChatGPT version/prompts/decoding, contamination checks, and per-source licensing remain undisclosed. EN/ZH specs preserve identical IDs, types, positions, and edges. Formal publication evidence [site-a11p-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 3469×1561 (English) and 3469×1561 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 3467×1559 and 3467×1559. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
